headline: Cross averages 114 as Clayton and Rock exit the Grand Slam
standfirst: Rob Cross beat Jonny Clayton 5-1 and Kevin Doets beat Josh Rock 5-3 as seeded players fell in Sunday's afternoon session in Wolverhampton.
body: Jonny Clayton and Josh Rock are out of the Grand Slam of Darts after a second-round afternoon session in Wolverhampton on Sunday that also ended the campaign of Luke Woodhouse.

Clayton, who had lost his opener to Anton Ostlund, was beaten 5-1 by Rob Cross in Group G. Cross averaged more than 114 and landed five checkouts in succession: 137, 138, 100, 91 and 76. He now plays Ostlund on Monday evening for a place in the last 16.

Rock had lost to Tommy Morris on the opening weekend, and a 5-3 defeat by Kevin Doets in Group C finished his chances. Doets averaged over 100, and he meets Morris on Monday to decide who goes through.
Woodhouse also paid for a first-game defeat against Tom Sykes. Krzysztof Ratajski beat him 5-1 in Group J, which sets up a Ratajski against Sykes decider.

Elsewhere, Maik Kuivenhoven came from 4-1 down to beat Karel Sedlacek 5-4 in Group P, which eliminated Kuivenhoven but leaves Sedlacek needing a big result against Nathan Aspinall. Cameron Menzies edged Raymond Smith 5-4 in Group D and plays Stephen Bunting next.

Alan Soutar beat Lisa Ashton 5-2 in Group B and will face Jermaine Wattimena in a shootout. Andrew Gilding beat Charlie Manby 5-4 with a 124 finish, and Niko Springer averaged almost 100 in a 5-1 win over Adam Sevada that sets up a meeting with Wessel Nijman for Group H.
